rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.3 and Tables 1-5 report a two-year rain-fed field experiment (randomized blocks, three replicates) measuring soil respiration, Q10, soil temperature and moisture, yield and biomass under winter wheat and spring maize with and without N fertilization.
rows.notes: The study contains no drip irrigation, no irrigation at all (rain-fed Loess Plateau cropland), no emitter spacing, irrigation scheduling or fertigation uniformity. It reports effects of crop type and broadcast urea N fertilization on soil respiration and its temperature sensitivity (Q10), plus yield and biomass responses to N. It provides no evidence on drip system management precision or uneven water/nutrient delivery constraining crop productivity. The citation appears misattributed (possibly confused with a different Wang et al., 2016).

notes: Full text appears complete. The study is a soil-respiration/Q10 field experiment under rain-fed wheat and maize with N fertilization; it has no relation to drip irrigation or irrigation management precision.
